post.caption: A diamond mine named Fat Lake. Geologist Stewart Blusson and prospector Chuck Fipke searched Canada's far north, following telltale minerals back along the paths glaciers took. In 1990, a bright green mineral turned up by a frozen lake, and mining giant BHP then joined them for a 51 percent share. In November 1991, they announced 81 small diamonds, which set off one of the greatest staking rushes in history. Ekati opened in October 1998 as Canada's first diamond mine, and Ekati is a local word that means Fat Lake. Each CanadaMark diamond is laser inscribed with its own serial number.
